sanskrit_verse:
भक्षैर् वा यदि वा भोज्यैर् वस्त्रैर् माल्यैस् तथैव च ।
संप्रेष्यमाणैर् गन्धैश् च सर्वं संग्रहणं स्मृतम् ॥
transliteration: bhakṣair vā yadi vā bhojyair vastrair mālyais tathaiva ca | saṃpreṣyamāṇair gandhaiś ca sarvaṃ saṃgrahaṇaṃ smṛtam ||
sph_interpretive_translation: All objects offered or sent—whether as edibles, consumables, garments, garlands, or scents—are to be received and integrated as expressions of dharmic exchange.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in the conscious acceptance of relational offerings
Causation arises through intentional transmission of material support
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to receive and integrate
Restoration logic operates through acknowledgment and completion of exchange
Consciousness alignment occurs when receipt is recognized as a sacred duty
executable_legal_axioms: IF an offering is transmitted with intent AND the recipient has capacity to receive THEN integration must occur without obstruction
IF an item is sent for dharmic purpose THEN refusal to accept disrupts relational dharma
IF material is offered in good faith THEN non-receipt obligates explanation within 24 hours
IF receipt occurs THEN recipient assumes completion responsibility for energetic and physical integration
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Adjudication, this verse establishes that refusal to acknowledge rightful offerings—especially those made for sustenance, honor, or spiritual upliftment—constitutes a breach of dharma at the highest level of societal function. Courts must recognize such refusals not as personal choices but as violations of systemic integrity requiring immediate restoration protocols.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that transmission creates relational obligation; anupūrvaśaḥ shows that refusal distorts sequential harmony; proportional responsibility lies in completing the exchange; non-punitive reality rule affirms that correction restores flow rather than inflicts harm.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate completion process wherein sender and receiver engage in formal acknowledgment ceremony
Assign responsibility assumption protocol where receiver publicly accepts and integrates offering
Implement capacity restoration mechanism through guided practice of gratitude and receptivity
Enforce integrity reintegration via community witnessing of renewed dharmic exchange
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: all offerings are sacred transmissions requiring conscious reception. Dharma is restored through recognition and integration. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
